title: What is five twelfths times seven eighteenths?
description: The video finds five twelfths times seven eighteenths by taking one twelfth of seven eighteenths and then five of those, which shows the tops multiply and the bottoms multiply. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that only the tops multiply.
teaching_notes: One idea: one twelfth of seven eighteenths is seven two hundred sixteenths, and five of those make thirty five two hundred sixteenths. Watch for students who multiply the tops and keep one bottom.

video_script.why: The child can multiply two fractions with one on top and now meets tops larger than one.
video_script.substitution: One twelfth of seven eighteenths is seven two hundred sixteenths, and five of those make thirty five two hundred sixteenths.
video_script.anchor: Find five twelfths times seven eighteenths
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the tops, five and seven, and keeps the bottom twelve, and gets thirty five twelfths, which is nearly three wholes
video_script.payoff_line: Five twelfths times seven eighteenths is thirty five two hundred sixteenths
video_script.fraction_reading: five twelfths, seven eighteenths, seven two hundred sixteenths, thirty five two hundred sixteenths, thirty five twelfths
maths_rules: cut 7/18 into 12 equal parts: the whole has 12 × 18 = 216 equal parts
in general, a/b × c/d = (a × c)/(b × d)
the slip: 35/12 is nearly 3, but the product of two fractions below 1 is below 1
video_script.design: One idea: take one twelfth of seven eighteenths, then five of those, and see that tops multiply and bottoms multiply. The unit square is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, cut seven eighteenths into twelve equal parts.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>The whole now has twelve times eighteen, which is two hundred sixteen equal parts.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, one twelfth of seven eighteenths is seven of these small parts.
That is seven small parts out of two hundred sixteen equal parts.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, five twelfths is five times one twelfth.
We take five copies of seven over two hundred sixteen.

marks.rule: (5 × 7)/(12 × 18) is written beside it with the tops and the bottoms marked
marks.pay: the answer stays on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five times seven is thirty five, so the answer has thirty five on top.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The tops multiply and the bottoms multiply.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Five twelfths times seven eighteenths is thirty five two hundred sixteenths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 5/12 × 7/18 = 35/12 is written and crossed out; 35/12 is drawn longer than one whole; the tops and the bottoms are marked

marks.fix: 35/12 is drawn longer than one whole and the line is crossed out
marks.rule: the bottoms 12 and 18 are multiplied to give 216

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is thirty five twelfths.
Keeko multiplied the tops, five and seven, and kept only one of the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But both fractions are less than one.
Their product must be smaller than each of them, but thirty five twelfths is nearly three wholes.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Multiply the tops, and multiply the bottoms too.
